Computer Fundamentals (Hardware & Softwa.question: 10) A computer cannot ''boot'' if it does not have the _____.
Computer Fundamentals (Hardware & Softwa.exp:
An operating system is the system software that handles the software and hardware resources and provides services for the computer programs.
So, without an operating system, a computer cannot ''boot''.

Computer Fundamentals (Hardware & Softwa.question: 11) The computer's processor consists of the following parts
Computer Fundamentals (Hardware & Softwa.option2: খ) Hard Disk and Floppy Drive
Computer Fundamentals (Hardware & Softwa.exp: The CPU is made up of three main components, the control unit , the immediate access store and the arithmetic and logic unit.

Computer Fundamentals (Hardware & Softwa.question: 12) Where is RAM located?
Computer Fundamentals (Hardware & Softwa.exp:
RAM is located in the central processing unit (CPU), also called a processor, is located inside the computer case on the motherboard.
It is sometimes called the brain of the computer, and its job is to carry out commands.

Computer Fundamentals (Hardware & Softwa.question: 13) Several computers linked to a server to share programs and storage space ________.
Computer Fundamentals (Hardware & Softwa.exp:
- A network consists of two or more computers that are linked in order to share resources.
- Integrated systems, or systems integration, are the process of bringing together component subsystems into one functional system.
- An operating system (OS) is system software that manages computer hardware, software resources, and provides common services for computer programs.

Computer Fundamentals (Hardware & Softwa.question: 18) The basic architecture of logical design of digital computers developed by-
Computer Fundamentals (Hardware & Softwa.exp: In 1945, Professor J. von Neumann, who was then working at the Moore School of Engineering in Philadelphia, where the E.N.I.A.C. had been built, issued on behalf of a group of his co-workers, a report on the logical design of digital computers.

Computer Fundamentals (Hardware & Softwa.question: 19) In Which generation was the microprocessor introduced?
Computer Fundamentals (Hardware & Softwa.exp:
The microprocessor brought the fourth generation of computers, as thousands of integrated circuits were built onto a single silicon chip.
What in the first generation filled an entire room could now fit in the palm of the hand.
The Intel 4004 chip, developed in 1971, located all the components of the computer from the Central processing Unit (CPU) and memory to input/output controls on a single chip.

These small computers became more powerful, they could be linked together to form networks, which eventually led to the development of the Internet. Fourth generation computers also saw the development of GUIs, the mouse and handheld devices

Computer Fundamentals (Hardware & Softwa.question: 20) Which of the following memories is non-volatile?
Computer Fundamentals (Hardware & Softwa.exp: Examples of non-volatile memory include read-only memory (see ROM), flash memory, most types of magnetic computer storage devices (e.g. hard disks, floppy discs and magnetic tape), optical discs, and early computer storage methods such as paper tape and punched cards

Computer Fundamentals (Hardware & Softwa.question: 21) An optical input device that interprets pencil mark on paper media is -
Computer Fundamentals (Hardware & Softwa.exp:
Magnetic audio tape is used to capture speech and music and video.
An optical scan voting system is an electronic voting system and uses an optical scanner to read marked paper ballots and tally the results.
A computer punched card reader or just computer card reader is a computer input device used to read computer programs.
Optical Mark reading (OMR) is a method of entering data into a computer system. Optical Mark Readers reads pencil or pen marks made in pre-defined positions on paper forms.

Computer Fundamentals (Hardware & Softwa.question: 22) What is cache RAM?
Computer Fundamentals (Hardware & Softwa.option1: ক) Extra memory used for overflow from your Hard Disk
Computer Fundamentals (Hardware & Softwa.option2: খ) A place to store secret information like passwords
Computer Fundamentals (Hardware & Softwa.option3: গ) It’s the same as your Hard Disk Drive
Computer Fundamentals (Hardware & Softwa.option4: ঘ) Fast memory used for data that is accessed often
Computer Fundamentals (Hardware & Softwa.exp: A cache is a smaller, faster memory, located closer to a processor core, which stores copies of the data from frequently used. So, the first three options are irrelevant.

Computer Fundamentals (Hardware & Softwa.question: 23) One nibble is equal to-
Computer Fundamentals (Hardware & Softwa.exp:
In computing, a nibble is a four-bit aggregation, or half an octet. It is also known as half-byte or tetrad.
One byte = 8 bits
One nibble = 4 bits

Computer Fundamentals (Hardware & Softwa.question: 24) A new presentation can be created from-
Computer Fundamentals (Hardware & Softwa.exp:

When you have already opened a new presentation you may start another new presentation by pressing Ctrl+N.

Computer Fundamentals (Hardware & Softwa.question: 25) Identify false statement.
Computer Fundamentals (Hardware & Softwa.option1: ক) You can find deleted files in recycle bin
Computer Fundamentals (Hardware & Softwa.option2: খ) You can restore any files from recycle bin if you need
Computer Fundamentals (Hardware & Softwa.option3: গ) You can increase free space of disk by sending files in recycle bin
Computer Fundamentals (Hardware & Softwa.option4: ঘ) You can right click and choose Empty Recycle Bin to clean it at once
Computer Fundamentals (Hardware & Softwa.exp:
In Windows, the Recycle Bin is a folder or directory where deleted items are temporarily stored.(তারমানে পুরোপুরি ডিলিট হয়ে যাচ্ছে না) 
Deleted files are not permanently removed from the hard drive but are sent instead to the Recycle Bin, unless they are too large.
The files in the Recycle Bin can be restored to their original location.

Computer Fundamentals (Hardware & Softwa.question: 29) Which of the following shut down methods is often called warm boot?
Computer Fundamentals (Hardware & Softwa.exp:

It may be used in contrast to a cold boot, which refers to starting up a computer that has been turned off.
